Tom Willander hasn't had a point in 13 straight games, and our numbers say that's mostly bad luck: about 3.8 expected points of chances in that stretch. He also missed games last week with a lower-body injury, a late scratch against Anaheim who stayed out in Winnipeg, per Sportsnet and The Hockey News.

The 11th pick of 2023, out of Boston University, is a little behind the curve for defensemen picked 6th to 16th, whose median first full season was 0.24 points a game. He's at 0.19. But the five-on-five picture is one of the better ones on the Canucks: Vancouver is nearly eight points of expected goal share better with him on the ice than off it.

The tools are there. NHL Edge has him faster than 93% of the league, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows him getting to the home-plate area in front of the net more than 83% of defensemen. Evolving-Hockey flagged his defense last season as a weakness, with weak teammates around him. Our range has him at 16 to 32 points over a full season. Health first; the points should start to come.
headline: Willander's drought is mostly luck
